newsitem.title: USA: Orthofix wins $150 mln civil action.
newsitem.headline: Orthofix wins $150 mln civil action.

text.p: Orthofix International NV on Monday said a federal jury in Camden, N.J., awarded three of its affiliates almost $150 million in damages in a breach-of-contract lawsuit against its former U.S. distributor.

Orthofix said in a news release its affiliates were awarded $48.9 million in compensatory damages and $100.6 million in punitive damages from EBI Medical Systems Inc and its parent companies, Electro-Biology Inc and Biomet.
Biomet said in a separate statement that it planned to appeal the jury verdict.
"Unfortunately, it appears that we have been unfairly penalized for our success in the marketplace following Orthofix's unwillingness to renew the distribution agreement with EBI," Biomet said.
EBI designed its own orthopedic medical device, since the distribution agreement with Orthofix was not renewed, Biomet said.

Orthofix, a maker of medical devices, said its suit alleged among other things that EBI Medical breached its distributor agreement by developing a competitive product during the term of the agreement.

Orthofix said the jury found for EBI Medical on certain of its counterclaims, which Orthofix did not specify. The jury awarded EBI compensatory damages of $2.00 and no punitive damages, Orthofix said.

Biomet said it has not made a decision about the amount of any provision or related liability after the verdict because a judgment has not yet been entered and the company planned to appeal the jury award.
Biomet said the outcome of the case would not have a material impact on its operations and that it would be able to pay any judgment through its cash, investments and cash flow.
